sanskrit: mataṅgavāpyāṃ yaḥ snāyād ekarātreṇa sidhyati vigāhati hy anālambam andhakaṃ vai sanātanam
english: He who bathes in the Mataṅga pool attains perfection in a single night; for he passes through the eternal, supportless, blinding darkness.

sanskrit: naimiṣe svargatīrthe ca upaspṛśya jitendriyaḥ phalaṃ puruṣamedhasya labhen māsaṃ kṛtodakaḥ
english: He who, with senses subdued, touches the waters at Naimiṣa and at the Svargatīrtha, and offers libations there for a month, wins the fruit of the Puruṣamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: gaṅgāhrada upaspṛśya tathā caivotpalāvane aśvamedham avāpnoti tatra māsaṃ kṛtodakaḥ
english: Touching the waters of the Gaṅgā-pool and likewise of the Utpalāvana, and offering libations there for a month, a man obtains the merit of the Horse Sacrifice.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyamunayos tīrthe tathā kālaṃjare girau ṣaṣṭihrada upaspṛśya dānaṃ nānyad viśiṣyate
english: At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, and upon Mount Kālaṃjara, touching the Ṣaṣṭi pool—no other gift surpasses what is gained there.

sanskrit: daśa tīrthasahasrāṇi tisraḥ koṭyas tathāparāḥ samāgacchanti māghyāṃ tu prayāge bharatarṣabha
english: Ten thousand sacred fords, and thirty million others besides, all gather at Prayāga in the month of Māgha, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: māghamāsaṃ prayāge tu niyataḥ saṃśitavrataḥ snātvā tu bharataśreṣṭha nirmalaḥ svargam āpnuyāt
english: He who, restrained and firm in his vows, bathes at Prayāga during the month of Māgha, O best of the Bharatas, becomes spotless and attains heaven.

sanskrit: marudgaṇa upaspṛśya pitṝṇām āśrame śuciḥ vaivasvatasya tīrthe ca tīrthabhūto bhaven naraḥ
english: Touching the waters at the Marudgaṇa, pure at the hermitage of the Fathers, and at the ford of Vaivasvata, a man himself becomes as holy as a sacred ford.

sanskrit: tathā brahmaśiro gatvā bhāgīrathyāṃ kṛtodakaḥ ekamāsaṃ nirāhāraḥ somalokam avāpnuyāt
english: So too, having gone to Brahmaśiras and offered libations in the Bhāgīrathī, fasting for one month, a man attains the world of Soma.

sanskrit: kapotake naraḥ snātvā aṣṭāvakre kṛtodakaḥ dvādaśāhaṃ nirāhāro naramedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: A man who bathes at Kapotaka and offers libations at Aṣṭāvakra, fasting for twelve days, wins the fruit of the Naramedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: muñjapṛṣṭhaṃ gayāṃ caiva nirṛtiṃ devaparvatam tṛtīyāṃ krauñcapādīṃ ca brahmahatyā viśudhyati
english: By visiting Muñjapṛṣṭha and Gayā, Nirṛti and the mountain of the gods, and thirdly the Krauñcapādī, even the slaying of a brāhmaṇa is purged away.

sanskrit: kalaśyāṃ vāpy upaspṛśya vedyāṃ ca bahuśojalām agneḥ pure naraḥ snātvā viśālāyāṃ kṛtodakaḥ devahrada upaspṛśya brahmabhūto virājate
english: Touching the waters at Kalaśī, and often at the Vedī, bathing at the city of Agni and offering libations at Viśālā, and touching the waters of the Devahrada, a man shines forth, having become one with Brahman.

sanskrit: purāpavartanaṃ nandāṃ mahānandāṃ ca sevya vai nandane sevyate dāntas tv apsarobhir ahiṃsakaḥ
english: Having resorted to Purāpavartana, the Nandā, and the Mahānandā, the self-controlled and harmless man is waited upon by the apsarases in the grove of Nandana.

sanskrit: urvaśīkṛttikāyoge gatvā yaḥ susamāhitaḥ lauhitye vidhivat snātvā puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet
english: He who, well-composed, goes there at the conjunction of Urvaśī and the Kṛttikā stars, and bathes in due form in the Lauhitya, wins the fruit of the Puṇḍarīka sacrifice.

sanskrit: rāmahrada upaspṛśya viśālāyāṃ kṛtodakaḥ dvādaśāhaṃ nirāhāraḥ kalmaṣād vipramucyate
english: Touching the waters of the Rāma-pool and offering libations at Viśālā, fasting for twelve days, a man is wholly freed from defilement.

sanskrit: mahāhrada upaspṛśya śuddhena manasā naraḥ ekamāsaṃ nirāhāro jamadagnigatiṃ labhet
english: Touching the waters of the Mahāhrada with a purified mind, fasting for one month, a man attains the realm reached by Jamadagni.

sanskrit: vindhye saṃtāpya cātmānaṃ satyasaṃdhas tv ahiṃsakaḥ ṣaṇmāsaṃ padam āsthāya māsenaikena śudhyati
english: Mortifying himself on the Vindhya, true to his word and harmless, standing on one spot for six months, he is purified in but a single month thereafter.

sanskrit: narmadāyām upaspṛśya tathā sūrpārakodake ekapakṣaṃ nirāhāro rājaputro vidhīyate
english: Touching the waters of the Narmadā and likewise the waters of Sūrpāraka, fasting for a fortnight, a man is ordained to be born a king's son.

sanskrit: jambūmārge tribhir māsaiḥ saṃyataḥ susamāhitaḥ ahorātreṇa caikena siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
english: At Jambūmārga, restrained and well-composed for three months, a man wins perfection in but a single day and night.

sanskrit: kokāmukhe vigāhyāpo gatvā caṇḍālikāśramam śākabhakṣaś cīravāsāḥ kumārīr vindate daśa
english: Plunging into the waters at Kokāmukha and going to the hermitage of Caṇḍālikā, living on herbs and clad in bark, a man obtains ten maidens.

sanskrit: vaivasvatasya sadanaṃ na sa gacchet kadā cana yasya kanyāhrade vāso devalokaṃ sa gacchati
english: He whose dwelling is at the Kanyā-pool never goes to the abode of Vaivasvata; rather, he attains the world of the gods.

sanskrit: prabhāse tv ekarātreṇa amāvāsyāṃ samāhitaḥ sidhyate 'tra mahābāho yo naro jāyate punaḥ
english: At Prabhāsa, in a single night on the new moon, the composed man attains perfection here, O mighty-armed one—the man who is born again.

sanskrit: ujjānaka upaspṛśya ārṣṭiṣeṇasya cāśrame piṅgāyāś cāśrame snātvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Touching the waters at Ujjānaka, at the hermitage of Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, and bathing at the hermitage of Piṅgā, a man is released from all sins.

sanskrit: kulyāyāṃ samupaspṛśya japtvā caivāghamarṣaṇam aśvamedham avāpnoti trirātropoṣitaḥ śuciḥ
english: Touching the waters at Kulyā and reciting the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn, fasting three nights and pure, a man obtains the merit of the Horse Sacrifice.

sanskrit: piṇḍāraka upaspṛśya ekarātroṣito naraḥ agniṣṭomam avāpnoti prabhātāṃ śarvarīṃ śuciḥ
english: Touching the waters at Piṇḍāraka and fasting for one night, a man, pure when the night brightens into dawn, obtains the merit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: tathā brahmasaro gatvā dharmāraṇyopaśobhitam puṇḍarīkam avāpnoti prabhātāṃ śarvarīṃ śuciḥ
english: So too, having gone to the Brahma-lake, adorned by the Dharma forest, a man, pure when the night brightens into dawn, obtains the merit of the Puṇḍarīka sacrifice.

sanskrit: maināke parvate snātvā tathā saṃdhyām upāsya ca kāmaṃ jitvā ca vai māsaṃ sarvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: Bathing on Mount Maināka and worshipping at the twilight hours, and conquering desire for a month, a man wins the fruit of the Sarvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: vikhyāto himavān puṇyaḥ śaṃkaraśvaśuro giriḥ ākaraḥ sarvaratnānāṃ siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ
english: Renowned and holy is the Himavat, the mountain that is Śaṃkara's father-in-law, the mine of all gems, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: śarīram utsṛjet tatra vidhipūrvam anāśake adhruvaṃ jīvitaṃ jñātvā yo vai vedāntago dvijaḥ
english: There the twice-born man who has reached the end of the Veda, knowing life to be impermanent, may lay down his body according to the rite, fasting unto death.

sanskrit: abhyarcya devatās tatra namaskṛtya munīṃs tathā tataḥ siddho divaṃ gacched brahmalokaṃ sanātanam
english: Having there worshipped the deities and bowed to the sages, he then, made perfect, goes to heaven, to the eternal world of Brahman.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca yo jitvā tīrtham āvaset na tena kiṃ cin na prāptaṃ tīrthābhigamanād bhavet
english: He who, having conquered desire, anger, and greed, dwells at a sacred ford—there is nothing he has not gained by his pilgrimage to that ford.

sanskrit: yāny agamyāni tīrthāni durgāṇi viṣamāṇi ca manasā tāni gamyāni sarvatīrthasamāsataḥ
english: Those sacred fords that are unreachable, hard of access, and perilous may be reached in the mind, by gathering together all the fords within oneself.

sanskrit: idaṃ medhyam idaṃ dhanyam idaṃ svargyam idaṃ sukham idaṃ rahasyaṃ devānām āplāvyānāṃ ca pāvanam
english: This is holy, this brings prosperity, this leads to heaven, this gives happiness; this is the secret of the gods, and the purifier of those who bathe.

sanskrit: idaṃ dadyād dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnām ātmajasya vā suhṛdāṃ ca japet karṇe śiṣyasyānugatasya vā
english: This one should impart to the twice-born, to the virtuous, or to one's own son; and one may whisper it in the ear of friends, or of a devoted disciple.

sanskrit: dattavān gautamasyedam aṅgirā vai mahātapāḥ gurubhiḥ samanujñātaḥ kāśyapena ca dhīmatā
english: This Aṅgiras of great austerity gave to Gautama, with the sanction of his teachers and of the wise Kāśyapa.

sanskrit: maharṣīṇām idaṃ japyaṃ pāvanānāṃ tathottamam japaṃś cābhyutthitaḥ śaśvan nirmalaḥ svargam āpnuyāt
english: This is the supreme prayer of the great purifying sages; reciting it, ever risen from sleep, a man becomes spotless and attains heaven.

sanskrit: idaṃ yaś cāpi śṛṇuyād rahasyaṃ tv aṅgiromatam uttame ca kule janma labhej jātiṃ ca saṃsmaret
english: And whoever hears this secret, the teaching of Aṅgiras, wins birth in an exalted family and remembers his former lives.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bṛhaspatisamaṃ buddhyā kṣamayā brahmaṇaḥ samam parākrame śakrasamam ādityasamatejasam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: His equal to Bṛhaspati in wisdom, like Brahmā in forbearance, equal to Śakra in valour, and matching the Sun in splendour—

sanskrit: gāṅgeyam arjunenājau nihataṃ bhūrivarcasam bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'nyaiś ca paryupāste yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: upon the son of Gaṅgā of abundant lustre, struck down by Arjuna in battle, Yudhiṣṭhira waited in attendance, together with his brothers and others.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ vīraśayane kālākāṅkṣiṇam acyutam ājagmur bharataśreṣṭhaṃ draṣṭukāmā maharṣayaḥ
english: To that best of the Bharatas, the unshaken one lying upon his hero's bed and awaiting his appointed hour, the great sages came, desiring to behold him.

sanskrit: atrir vasiṣṭho 'tha bhṛguḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ aṅgirā gautamo 'gastyaḥ sumatiḥ svāyur ātmavān
english: Atri, Vasiṣṭha, and Bhṛgu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Aṅgiras, Gautama, Agastya, Sumati, Svāyu the self-possessed,

sanskrit: viśvāmitraḥ sthūlaśirāḥ saṃvartaḥ pramatir damaḥ uśanā bṛhaspatir vyāsaś cyavanaḥ kāśyapo dhruvaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra, Sthūlaśiras, Saṃvarta, Pramati, Dama, Uśanas, Bṛhaspati, Vyāsa, Cyavana, Kāśyapa, Dhruva,

sanskrit: durvāsā jamadagniś ca mārkaṇḍeyo 'tha gālavaḥ bharadvājaś ca raibhyaś ca yavakrītas tritas tathā
english: Durvāsas and Jamadagni, Mārkaṇḍeya and Gālava, Bharadvāja and Raibhya, Yavakrīta and likewise Trita,

sanskrit: sthūlākṣaḥ śakalākṣaś ca kaṇvo medhātithiḥ kṛśaḥ nāradaḥ parvataś caiva sudhanvāthaikato dvitaḥ
english: Sthūlākṣa and Śakalākṣa, Kaṇva, Medhātithi, Kṛśa, Nārada and Parvata, Sudhanvan, and then Ekata and Dvita,

sanskrit: nitaṃbhūr bhuvano dhaumyaḥ śatānando 'kṛtavraṇaḥ jāmadagnyas tathā rāmaḥ kāmyaś cety evamādayaḥ samāgatā mahātmāno bhīṣmaṃ draṣṭuṃ maharṣayaḥ
english: Nitaṃbhū, Bhuvana, Dhaumya, Śatānanda, Akṛtavraṇa, and Rāma the son of Jamadagni, and Kāmya, and others such as these—great-souled sages all, gathered to behold Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ mahātmanāṃ pūjām āgatānāṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaś cakre yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ
english: To those great-souled ones who had come, Yudhiṣṭhira, together with his brothers, paid homage in due form, one after another.

sanskrit: te pūjitāḥ sukhāsīnāḥ kathāś cakrur maharṣayaḥ bhīṣmāśritāḥ sumadhurāḥ sarvendriyamanoharāḥ
english: Thus honoured and seated at ease, the great sages held discourse—discourse centred upon Bhīṣma, most sweet, and delighting every sense.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas teṣāṃ kathāḥ śrutvā ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām mene divistham ātmānaṃ tuṣṭyā paramayā yutaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, hearing the discourse of those sages of disciplined soul, deemed himself already dwelling in heaven, filled with the highest contentment.

sanskrit: tatas te bhīṣmam āmantrya pāṇḍavāṃś ca maharṣayaḥ antardhānaṃ gatāḥ sarve sarveṣām eva paśyatām
english: Then those great sages, taking leave of Bhīṣma and the Pāṇḍavas, all vanished from sight while everyone looked on.

sanskrit: tān ṛṣīn sumahābhāgān antardhānagatān api pāṇḍavās tuṣṭuvuḥ sarve praṇemuś ca muhur muhuḥ
english: Those most blessed sages, though they had vanished, the Pāṇḍavas all praised, and bowed to them again and again.

sanskrit: prasannamanasaḥ sarve gāṅgeyaṃ kurusattamāḥ upatasthur yathodyantam ādityaṃ mantrakovidāḥ
english: With serene minds, those best of the Kurus, skilled in sacred verses, attended upon the son of Gaṅgā as upon the rising Sun.

sanskrit: prabhāvāt tapasas teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ vīkṣya pāṇḍavāḥ prakāśanto diśaḥ sarvā vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ
english: Beholding, through the power of their austerities, those sages illumining all the quarters of the sky, the Pāṇḍavas were filled with the utmost wonder.

sanskrit: mahābhāgyaṃ paraṃ teṣām ṛṣīṇām anucintya te pāṇḍavāḥ saha bhīṣmeṇa kathāś cakrus tadāśrayāḥ
english: Reflecting upon the supreme greatness of those sages, the Pāṇḍavas, together with Bhīṣma, made them the subject of their discourse.

sanskrit: kathānte śirasā pādau spṛṣṭvā bhīṣmasya pāṇḍavaḥ dharmyaṃ dharmasutaḥ praśnaṃ paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: At the close of the talk, the son of Dharma, touching Bhīṣma's feet with his head, put to him a question concerning dharma—Yudhiṣṭhira, the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: ke deśāḥ ke janapadā āśramāḥ ke ca parvatāḥ prakṛṣṭāḥ puṇyataḥ kāś ca jñeyā nadyaḥ pitāmaha
english: Which lands, which realms, which hermitages, and which mountains are most excellent in holiness; and which rivers should be known as such, O grandsire?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śiloñchavṛtteḥ saṃvādaṃ siddhasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point, too, they tell an ancient tale, the dialogue between one who lived by gleaning ears of grain and a Siddha, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: imāṃ kaś cit parikramya pṛthivīṃ śailabhūṣitām asakṛd dvipadāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhasya gṛhamedhinaḥ
english: A certain man, best among bipeds, having wandered again and again over this earth adorned with mountains, came to the house of an excellent householder—

sanskrit: śilavṛtter gṛhaṃ prāptaḥ sa tena vidhinārcitaḥ kṛtakṛtya upātiṣṭhat siddhaṃ tam atithiṃ tadā
english: he reached the home of the gleaner, who, having fulfilled his duty, honoured him in due form and then attended upon that Siddha as his guest.

sanskrit: tau sametya mahātmānau sukhāsīnau kathāḥ śubhāḥ cakratur vedasaṃbaddhās taccheṣakṛtalakṣaṇāḥ
english: Those two great souls, meeting and seated at ease, held auspicious discourse bound up with the Veda and marked by what completes its purport.

sanskrit: śilavṛttiḥ kathānte tu siddham āmantrya yatnataḥ praśnaṃ papraccha medhāvī yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: At the close of the talk, the gleaner, an intelligent man, earnestly addressed the Siddha and asked him the very question that you now ask of me:

sanskrit: śilavṛttir uvāca ke deśāḥ ke janapadāḥ ke ''śramāḥ ke ca parvatāḥ prakṛṣṭāḥ puṇyataḥ kāś ca jñeyā nadyas tad ucyatām
english: The gleaner said: Which lands, which realms, which hermitages, and which mountains are most excellent in holiness; and which rivers should be known as such—let that be told.

sanskrit: siddha uvāca te deśās te janapadās te ''śramās te ca parvatāḥ yeṣāṃ bhāgīrathī gaṅgā madhyenaiti saridvarā
english: The Siddha said: Those lands, those realms, those hermitages, and those mountains are most excellent through whose midst the Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā, best of rivers, flows.

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa yajñais tyāgena vā punaḥ gatiṃ tāṃ na labhej jantur gaṅgāṃ saṃsevya yāṃ labhet
english: That goal which a creature attains by resorting to the Gaṅgā, he could not win even by austerity, by chastity, by sacrifices, or again by renunciation.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭāni yeṣāṃ gāṅgeyais toyair gātrāṇi dehinām nyastāni na punas teṣāṃ tyāgaḥ svargād vidhīyate
english: Those embodied beings whose limbs have been touched and laid to rest by the waters of the Gaṅgā—for them no expulsion from heaven is ever ordained.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi yeṣāṃ gāṅgeyais toyaiḥ kṛtyāni dehinām gāṃ tyaktvā mānavā vipra divi tiṣṭhanti te 'calāḥ
english: Those men all of whose rites have been performed with the waters of the Gaṅgā, O brāhmaṇa, having left the earth, abide unshaken in heaven.

sanskrit: pūrve vayasi karmāṇi kṛtvā pāpāni ye narāḥ paścād gaṅgāṃ niṣevante te 'pi yānty uttamāṃ gatim
english: Those men who, having done evil deeds in their earlier years, afterward resort to the Gaṅgā—they too attain the highest goal.

sanskrit: snātānāṃ śucibhis toyair gāṅgeyaiḥ prayatātmanām vyuṣṭir bhavati yā puṃsāṃ na sā kratuśatair api
english: The fruit that comes to men of disciplined soul who have bathed in the pure waters of the Gaṅgā—that comes not even from a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: yāvad asthi manuṣyasya gaṅgātoyeṣu tiṣṭhati tāvad varṣasahasrāṇi svargaṃ prāpya mahīyate
english: For as many thousands of years as a man's bone rests in the waters of the Gaṅgā, so long does he, having attained heaven, abide there in honour.

sanskrit: apahatya tamas tīvraṃ yathā bhāty udaye raviḥ tathāpahatya pāpmānaṃ bhāti gaṅgājalokṣitaḥ
english: As the sun, scattering the dense darkness at its rising, shines forth, so, scattering his sin, shines the man sprinkled with the waters of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: visomā iva śarvaryo vipuṣpās taravo yathā tadvad deśā diśaś caiva hīnā gaṅgājalaiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: As nights are without the moon, as trees are without blossom, so are the lands and the regions that are bereft of the holy waters of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: varṇāśramā yathā sarve svadharmajñānavarjitāḥ kratavaś ca yathāsomās tathā gaṅgāṃ vinā jagat
english: As all the castes and stages of life would be, were they stripped of the knowledge of their own duty, and as sacrifices would be without the Soma—so is the world without the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: yathā hīnaṃ nabho 'rkeṇa bhūḥ śailaiḥ khaṃ ca vāyunā tathā deśā diśaś caiva gaṅgāhīnā na saṃśayaḥ
english: As the sky would be without the sun, the earth without mountains, and space without wind, so are the lands and regions that lack the Gaṅgā—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu ye ke cit prāṇinaḥ sarva eva te tarpyamāṇāḥ parāṃ tṛptiṃ yānti gaṅgājalaiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: Whatever living beings there are in the three worlds, all of them, when refreshed with the holy waters of the Gaṅgā, attain the highest satisfaction.

sanskrit: yas tu sūryeṇa niṣṭaptaṃ gāṅgeyaṃ pibate jalam gavāṃ nirhāranirmuktād yāvakāt tad viśiṣyate
english: He who drinks the water of the Gaṅgā warmed by the sun gains more than from barley-gruel freed of the cattle's dung-fuel.

sanskrit: induvratasahasraṃ tu cared yaḥ kāyaśodhanam pibed yaś cāpi gaṅgāmbhaḥ samau syātāṃ na vā samau
english: Whether a man perform for a thousand lunar fasts the cleansing of the body, or whether he drink the water of the Gaṅgā—whether these two be equal or not equal, who can say?

sanskrit: tiṣṭhed yugasahasraṃ tu pādenaikena yaḥ pumān māsam ekaṃ tu gaṅgāyāṃ samau syātāṃ na vā samau
english: Whether a man stand for a thousand ages upon a single foot, or whether he dwell but one month by the Gaṅgā—whether these two be equal or not equal, who can say?

sanskrit: lambetāvākśirā yas tu yugānām ayutaṃ pumān tiṣṭhed yatheṣṭaṃ yaś cāpi gaṅgāyāṃ sa viśiṣyate
english: Though a man hang head-downward for ten thousand ages, yet he who dwells at the Gaṅgā as he pleases surpasses him.

sanskrit: agnau prāptaṃ pradhūyeta yathā tūlaṃ dvijottama tathā gaṅgāvagāḍhasya sarvaṃ pāpaṃ pradhūyate
english: As cotton cast into the fire is burnt utterly away, O best of the twice-born, so all the sin of one who plunges into the Gaṅgā is burnt away.

sanskrit: bhūtānām iha sarveṣāṃ duḥkhopahatacetasām gatim anveṣamāṇānāṃ na gaṅgāsadṛśī gatiḥ
english: For all beings here whose minds are stricken with sorrow and who seek a refuge, there is no refuge like the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: bhavanti nirviṣāḥ sarpā yathā tārkṣyasya darśanāt gaṅgāyā darśanāt tadvat sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: As serpents are rendered venomless at the sight of Tārkṣya, so by the sight of the Gaṅgā a man is released from all his sins.

sanskrit: apratiṣṭhāś ca ye ke cid adharmaśaraṇāś ca ye teṣāṃ pratiṣṭhā gaṅgeha śaraṇaṃ śarma varma ca
english: To whatever beings are without support, and to whatever beings take refuge in unrighteousness, the Gaṅgā here is their support, their refuge, their comfort, and their armour.
